column2: Thus addressed by the Lotus-seated, reflecting with intellect, the best of Brahmins gave up his anger and said to the lord of the gods what had been done to Mohini's body:

God, your daughter Mohini is full of much sin; therefore she has no place in the worlds crowded with living beings.
naradapuran:160:49	Having reflected long, I have thought about Mohini; out of love for you I shall give it, for you are more worthy of honour to me.
naradapuran:160:50	As your word is true, so is mine too, O lord of the gods; the work of the gods will be done, and what Mohini did too.
naradapuran:160:51	Where the throngs of beings have not intruded, in that place Mohini shall stay. The earth with its continents is always pervaded by moving and unmoving beings,
naradapuran:160:52	the nether regions by demons and the like, the sky by birds and the like, heaven by souls of merit, the hells by those of sinful deeds,
naradapuran:160:53	the oceans by fish and the like; therefore there is no standing place for her. Then Brahma, having consulted all the gods, O best of kings,
said to the goddess Mohini: "You have no place anywhere." Hearing those words, Mohini, obeying her father's command,
the destroyer of Hari's day, bowed and said to all, in the company of the priest, to the gods, witnesses of the world:

O best of the thirty gods, I have folded my hands to you; with a gracious heart, gods, even with a hundred prostrations,
naradapuran:160:57	what I asked should be given to me, to please all. By the power of Ekadashi the goal of all sinners
naradapuran:160:58	is accomplished; so, best of gods, for increase of my purpose — husband, co-wife and son were made by me to go to Vaikuntha.
naradapuran:160:59	On earth I live as a widow and the like for your sake, so that Hari's day, O honourers, may seem evil to me.
naradapuran:160:60	I ask this; give it for my own purpose, otherwise not.

Leaving her — the enjoyment of union with her beloved — she, standing at his feet in invisible form, your name, wide-eyed one, is true: people say 'Mohini'.
naradapuran:161:27	Having bewildered all the people, you make a writing on my ledger. Having said so, the son of Vivasvan, delighted, bowed to the daughter of Brahma
and went with the gods to the world of heaven, taking the ledger-writer by the hand. When the gods had gone, Mohini approached Brahma, lord of gods and demons,
and informed him: "Father, this priest of mine is exceedingly fierce in anger; my body is burned, Lord of the world. Do something so that I may attain a body again.
I bewildered this world; at the end, standing on Yama's tithi (Ekadashi), the king long ago conquered Yama; by your power, father, he was made victorious.
This is your work, father, that again I be embodied, Lord of the world; console the Brahmin."
Hearing Mohini's words, Brahma, maker of the worlds' order, again consoled the Brahmin for his daughter's sake:

Vasu, dear, understand this which I say for your benefit and hers, great-fortuned, and for the good of all the worlds.
naradapuran:161:34	By you Mohini was reduced to ash in anger; she asks for a body again; give your command, honourer.
naradapuran:161:35	My daughter is your sacrificer; she is going to a bad end, dear. She is protected by you and me; she has done her task and practised austerity.
naradapuran:161:36	If you, honourer, inform me with a pure heart, then I, her father, shall again produce a body for her.
naradapuran:161:37	But she is the enemy of Vishnu's day, a doer of sin. As she may become pure, O best of Brahmins, let that be done at once.
Hearing Brahma's word, that priest gladly ordered a body for the sacrificer.
Hearing the Brahmin's word, Brahma, grandfather of the world, sprinkled the ashes of Mohini's body with water from his water-pot.
When sprinkled by Brahma, maker of the worlds, Mohini became embodied; bowing to her father and to the priest Vasu, she took their feet, bowing humbly.
Then Vasu, the king's priest, glad, said to his sacrificer — fair-hipped Mohini, abandoned by her master's son and widowed (heroless) —
Vasu said: "Goddess, anger has been given up by me at Brahma's word. I shall make a goal for you by bathing at holy places and similar rites."
Having said so to Mohini, the Brahmin, gladly bowing, dismissed Brahma, Lord of the worlds, father of Mohini.
Dismissed by Mohini and Vasu with love, Brahma went to the world beyond darkness by the unmanifest path.
That Vasu, best of Brahmins, priest of Rukmangada, thinking Mohini worthy of favour, reflected in his heart,
and after a moment's meditation understood the cause of her goal.
Bathing in and drinking (Ganga water), one purifies the family to the seventh generation, seven lower, seven higher, and seven beyond them.
The Ganga saves men even when merely mentioned in passing. Even he who without faith utters the name of the Ganga,
the holy river, becomes a vessel of heaven. Whatever his condition, even devoid of all dharma,
by praising the Ganga alone he would obtain an auspicious goal. Whether a slayer of a Brahmin, teacher or cow, or touched by all sins,
a man touching Ganga water is freed from all sins. "When shall I see that Ganga? When shall I get a bath?"
Thus desired by a man, she saves a hundred of his family. Now I shall tell you, goddess, the fruit of bathing in the Ganga,
hearing which one is freed from all sins, without doubt. For one who bathes in Ganga water, sin is at once destroyed,
and unprecedented merit is at once obtained, Mohini. For those who bathed in pure Ganga waters, with restrained self,
the merit that men have is not equalled even by hundreds of sacrifices. As the sun at rising shines, driving away intense darkness,
so one sprinkled with Ganga water shines, having driven away sin. Even by one single rite of bathing, O king's beauty,
a mortal in the Ganga surely obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice. Sin born over many births is destroyed for a man,
and by mere bathing in the Ganga he at once becomes a vessel of merit. Sin done in other places is destroyed on the Ganga bank;
sin done on the Ganga bank is destroyed by bathing in the Ganga. By day, night and at twilights, with effort in the Ganga,
having bathed, the merit of a horse-sacrifice, even in one's home with water brought from there; the merit in all holy places and all desired shrines
a mortal obtains from bathing in the Ganga, without doubt. Whether joined with great sins or all sins,
by bathing in the Ganga by rule one is freed from all sins. There has been and will be no bath better than a bath in the Ganga.
Especially in the Kali age Jahnavi removes sin. Having destroyed the faults born of desire, produced by body, speech and mind,
by bathing in the Ganga with devotion he rejoices in heaven like a god. The man who with devotion bathes in the Ganga for a year
has a stay for a kalpa in Vishnu's world, without doubt. The man who bathes in the Ganga always until death
is freed from all sins, with his whole family, with all enjoyments, and is honoured in Vishnu's world.
For two parardhas, no doubt is to be made: the mortal who constantly bathes in the Ganga without interruption
is liberated while living, and when dead goes to Vishnu's abode. The merit of bathing at noon is held ten times that of the morning bath;
in the evening a hundredfold, and endless in the presence of Shiva. Bathing in the Ganga surpasses a gift of ten million tawny cows.
Wherever the Ganga is bathed in is equal to Kurukshetra; at Haridvara, Prayaga and the confluence with the Indus the fruit is greater.
Those who bathe, O Jahnavi, in water heated by my rays pierce the circle and go to liberation — so says the Sun's word.
He who, though staying in his own house, praises you at the time of bathing will also go to heaven — thus Varuna said to her.
Having reached the Ganga bank on the Dark thirteenth of Madhu (Chaitra) with the Shatabhisha star, a day with ten crore moons and suns, if gained on the Ganga it equals hundreds of solar eclipses.

In the month of Jyeshtha, on a Tuesday, on the tenth of the bright half, in Hasta, this Jahnavi came down from the mountain to the world of mortals; on that tithi she removes sin — the Dashahara Ganga; she gives merit a hundred times that of the horse-sacrifice.
The heaps of great sins and sins that I have — having reached Govinda-Dvadashi, destroy them, O Jahnavi.
When the full-disc moon joins Jupiter in the star named Magha, that is held the greatness of the tithi.
If that is obtained on the Ganga, it equals hundreds of solar eclipses. Now the fruit of bathing by special place is told:
bathing in the Ganga wherever is ten times that at Kurukshetra; a hundred times Kurukshetra where it joins the Vindhya;
at Kashi the Jahnavi is said to be a hundred times the Vindhya. The Ganga is hard to get everywhere, greater at three places:
Gangadvara, Prayaga and the confluence of the Ganga and the ocean. Those who bathe in these go to heaven; those who die there are not reborn.
Hear the fruit of bathing at Gangadvara, Kushavarta: the fruit of seven Rajasuyas and two horse-sacrifices;
staying there half a month, the fruit of six Vishvajit sacrifices; the wise know the merit of the gift of a hundred thousand cows.
Then at Sarottama (Saptasarovara), Govinda, and Rudra at Kanakhala: bathing in the Ganga there one obtains imperishable merit.
The holy place named Saukara, of great merit, hear, auspicious one: where Achyuta appeared long ago in boar form —
one gets the merit of a hundred Agnichayanas, two Jyotishtomas, and the fruit of a thousand Agnishtomas.
At the Brahma tirtha there too, a man who bathes obtains the merit of ten thousand Jyotishtomas and three horse-sacrifices.
The sinless holy place named Kubja, where all diseases are destroyed and sin born from all births too, Mohini.
Another is here, the Kapila tirtha, where a man who bathes obtains fruit equal to giving ten thousand tawny cows.
Having bathed at Gangadvara, Kushavarta, Bilvaka, Nilaparvata and Kanakhala, one goes to heaven with sin shaken off.
Then for purification, a tirtha best of all holy places: bathing there a man obtains merit of two Vishvajits.
Then the holy place Venirajya, where the Sarayu met the Ganga, like a sister meeting a sister, holy and very meritorious.
From washing Hari's right lotus foot the river of the gods (Ganga), or the Sarayu born from his left foot, or born from the Manasa lake —
at that tirtha, worshipping Rudra and Vishnu, one attains Vishnu-hood. Bathing there is declared to give the fruit of five horse-sacrifices.
Then the Gandava tirtha, where the Gandaki met; a gift of a thousand cows and bathing there are equal.
Then the Rama-tirtha, holy, where Vaikuntha is near; then the Soma-tirtha, holy, where the sage Nakula
worshipped Shiva, meditated, and became one of his ganas. The holy place named Champaka, where the Ganga flows north,
equals Manikarnika and destroys great sins. Then the tirtha called Kalasha, where the sage rose from a pot —
Agastya, worshipping Rudra there, became the best of sages. Somadvipa, very holy, equal to Varanasi,
where Soma, worshipping the Lord, was borne on Rudra's head; where Vishvamitra's sister met the Ganga —
a man who bathes there becomes Indra's dear guest. A mortal bathing in the great holy place Jahnuhrada, Mohini,
surely becomes the saviour of twenty-one generations. And the Aditi-tirtha, where Aditi obtained Hari
from Kashyapa — bathing there, auspicious one, they say brings great prosperity. The great holy place Shiloccaya, where creatures, practising austerity,
go to heaven with the grass and all, by taking refuge in the host of holy places. The Indrani tirtha, where Indrani
practised austerity and got Indra as husband — it is to be served like Prayaga. The merit-giving Snataka tirtha, where Vishvamitra, practising austerity,
obtained the state of Brahmin sage as a Kshatriya by service to the holy place. The Pradyumna tirtha, famed for austerity, where Hari's Kama became his son named Pradyumna — great prosperity there.
Then Daksha-Prayaga, where the Yamuna comes from the Ganga:
having bathed there one obtains imperishable merit as at Prayaga.
One who offers arghya once with Ganga water, with special substances, in a copper vessel measuring a Magadha prastha,
to the gods along with his ancestors, with sons and grandsons, reaches heaven. Water, milk, kusha tips, ghee, curd and honey,
red karavira flowers and red sandal: this eight-limbed arghya is declared for the Sun.
The best of men who makes an installation of Vishnu, Shiva, the Sun, Durga or Brahma on the Ganga bank,
or has temples of them built as able, gets a crore times the merit of doing it in other holy places.
Making lingas as able from clay from the Ganga bank, with fine marks, installing them each day,
and worshipping them with mantras, leaves, flowers and the like as able, then throwing them daily into the Ganga: his merit is endless.
The best of men who in the Ganga, giver of all bliss, chants the eight-syllable mantra with devotion has liberation in his hand.
Chanting "Om namo Narayanaya" restrained, for six months, all successes attend him.
One who chants "Om namah Shivaya" with Om, by rule, twenty-four lakhs of times, is directly Shankara.
The five-syllable is the perfected knowledge, Shiva himself, without doubt. Pure or impure, one chanting it is sinless.
When the Ganga is worshipped, all gods are worshipped; therefore with all effort one should worship the river of the gods.
Four-armed, three-eyed, adorned with all limbs, with a jewelled pot, white lotus and the hands of boon and protection, auspicious,
clothed in white, adorned with pearls and gems, very gracious, fair-faced, her heart-lotus wet with mercy,
flooding the earth's surface with nectar, always bowed to by the three worlds — meditating on the Ganga as made of water, one who worships becomes a sharer of merit.
The man who thus worships constantly for even half a month is like a god, with much more fruit in time.
On the bright seventh of Vaishakha long ago Jahnu drank the Jahnavi in anger and released her again from his right ear.
One should worship the Goddess Ganga, whose girdle is the sky, there; and on the Akshaya (third) in Vaishakha and in Kartika, auspicious one,
having kept a night vigil with barley food and sesame, one should worship Vishnu, Ganga and Shambhu with devotion,
likewise with fragrant flowers, saffron, aloe and sandal, tulsi and bilva leaves, citron fruit and the like,
with incense, lamps and offerings in abundance as able, for thousands of crores of kalpas and hundreds of crores of kalpas,
he is honoured in Vishnu's world, seated on a divine aerial car. Then reaching the earth he becomes a righteous king,
enjoying many kinds of happiness, endowed with beauty, conduct and virtues; at the end of the body, becoming a knower, he obtains union with Shiva.
Sacrifice, gift, austerity, chanting, shraddha and worship of gods done on the Ganga become ten million times more.
Hear the fruit of merit of one who on the Akshaya-tritiya gives a ghee-cow on the Ganga bank by rule:
for thousands of crores of kalpas and hundreds of crores of kalpas, bright as a thousand suns, endowed with all desires,
in a variegated aerial car of gold and jewels adorned with swans, with his own ancestors, he is honoured in Brahma's world.
Then he is born as a Brahmin rich in wealth on the Ganga bank, and at the end, becoming a knower of Brahman, he attains liberation, without doubt.
So too one who gives a cow by rule is honoured in heaven for as many years as there are hairs on the cow.
Afterward he is born in a family crowded with wealth and grain, full of jewels, gold and land, endowed with conduct, learning and fame;
having enjoyed vast pleasures, joined with sons and grandsons, he becomes a sharer in liberation; no question need be made.
If a tawny cow is given by rule to a master of the Veda, she takes all his ancestors in hell to heaven.
One who on the Ganga bank gives a plot of land of a "nivartana" measure becomes superior to Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva for years equal to the number of the land's dust particles,
and is born again on earth, becoming lord of the seven continents. Awakened by the sounds of drums and conches, songs and instruments,
and the praises of bards, he who slept awakens; having obtained all happiness here, devoted to all dharma,
having taken all his ancestors in hell to heaven and freed those in heaven, he himself becomes a knower, Mohini,
and at the end, cutting with the sword of knowledge the fivefold ignorance, attains supreme dispassion and reaches the Supreme Brahman.
By a rod of seven cubits, thirty rods make a nivartana; a cow-hide measure is less a third; so Brahma himself declares the measure.
One who gives a village to Brahmins on the Ganga bank, for the pleasure of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Durga and the Sun,
whatever merit is in all gifts, whatever fruit in all sacrifices, and whatever fruit is declared in austerities, vows and holy deeds —
that is to be known as multiplied a thousandfold for the giver of a village. In a Vaishnava city, in an aerial car bright as ten million suns,
or in Shankara's, he plays, praised joyfully by the gods and others. Having stayed there for a time equal to the dust of the land,
he is born in the family of yogis endowed with qualities like anima. On the Akshaya, goddess, one who gives to the best Brahmin sixteen months' worth of gold
is also honoured in the worlds. By food-gift one reaches Vishnu's world; by sesame-gift Shiva's;
by gift of jewels Brahma's; by cow and gold Indra's; by gold and garments the Gandharva world; fame by gift of a maiden.
Having obtained learning, which gives liberation, knowledge, he goes to the stainless. The man who on the Ganga bank with devotion
has a garden made, joined with many kinds of trees, and a house with a grove, with plantains, coconuts, kapittha, ashoka, champaka,
jackfruit, bilva, kadamba, ashvattha, patala, mango, palm, orange trees and other trees,
with jasmine and vijaya, shining with patala, thus a thick dwelling beautified with flowers,
and gives it with devotion to Shiva, Vishnu, Durga or the Sun, having arranged all that is needed —
I shall tell the fruit of his merit in brief, not at length: as many as are the flowers, roots and fruits of those trees,
and the various seeds and their roots, so many thousands of kalpas does he stay in the worlds.
The first is the jaggery-cow, the second the ghee-cow, the third the sesame-cow, the fourth the water-cow,
the fifth the milk-cow, the sixth is remembered as the honey-cow, the seventh the sugar-cow, the eighth the curd-cow.
